title: Object Oriented Programming
description: Object-oriented programming taught in C# (and, in recent papers, Java): programming languages and the .NET framework, C# program structure and syntax, data types, variables and type conversion, decision making and loops, classes, encapsulation and methods, and constructors, inheritance and polymorphism. Built from the CSC 235 lecture slides (Introduction to C# Programming Language, weeks 1 to 12) and the C# Quick Guide filed with them.

topics.title: Programming Languages, C# and .NET
topics.summary: A programming language is a set of rules for communicating an algorithm, with its own syntax; languages have evolved through five generations and several paradigms. C# is Microsoft's modern object-oriented language designed with the .NET framework, whose runtime runs its programs.
subtopics: What a programming language is: syntax and semantics
A short history: FORTRAN to Java
The .NET framework, CLI, CLR and JIT

topics.title: C# Program Structure and Basic Syntax
topics.summary: A C# program has a namespace declaration, a class, methods, attributes, a Main method, statements and expressions, and comments. C# is case sensitive, statements end with semicolons, and identifiers follow fixed naming rules.
subtopics: The Hello World program line by line
Rules: case sensitivity, semicolons and Main
Naming styles: camel, Pascal and Hungarian

topics.title: Data Types, Variables and Type Conversion
topics.summary: C# variables are value types, which hold data directly, reference types, which refer to a memory location, or pointer types. Values convert between types implicitly when safe, or explicitly with a cast.
subtopics: Reference types: object, dynamic and string

topics.title: Decision Making and Loops
topics.summary: Decision-making structures test conditions to choose which statements run: if, if...else, nested if, switch and the ?: operator. Loops repeat statements: while, for, do...while and nested loops, controlled by break and continue.

topics.title: Classes, Encapsulation and Methods
topics.summary: In object-oriented programming a program is made of interacting objects; objects of the same kind belong to a class with member variables and methods. Encapsulation hides implementation details using access specifiers, and methods group statements that perform tasks.
subtopics: Access specifiers: public, private, protected, internal

topics.title: Constructors, Inheritance and Polymorphism
topics.summary: Constructors initialise new objects and destructors clean up when objects go out of scope. Inheritance defines a class in terms of another (an IS-A relationship); polymorphism, static through overloading and dynamic through abstract and virtual methods, gives one interface many functions.
subtopics: Abstract classes, sealed classes and interfaces
